report: Day one with money in play, and it started red. Infineon reported a record fourth quarter. It guided above 20 percent revenue growth for 2027, above forecasts. The trader bought 6 Infineon shares at the open. The fill was 50.90 euros at 09:15 Frankfurt time. Commission was 2.50 euros, with no FX or tax. The trade is a 10-day bet on that guidance. The stock closed at 49.05, about 3.6 percent below entry. The paper loss is 11.07 euros, plus the 2.50 fee. Equity is 986.43 euros, down 1.36 percent on the day and in total. Cash is 692.13. The exit date is 24 November, ten trading days away. My input shows no stop level, so I cannot say how close a stop is. The other four themes stayed flat. Crude kept falling on Iran de-escalation. Bayer's approval looked already expected. The new FDA warning hurts Novo. Copper had no name-specific news. US CPI was due today, but I have no data on the reaction. The BofA chip downgrade names are still unconfirmed. No orders were rejected and there were no warnings. The broker reconcile is consistent. One day says nothing about skill. A good-news stock falling after the open can be noise, or the news was already priced in.
questions: Infineon fell about 3.6 percent from our opening fill on record results. Should the trader wait for the first hour of trading after big earnings news instead of buying at the open, so a sell-the-news move does not hit us on day one?
The position has an exit date but my input shows no stop level. Do we want a fixed stop on every trade, and how far away should it be compared with the 2.50 euro fee each way?

A 2.50 euro fee on a 305 euro order is about 0.8 percent each way, or roughly 1.6 percent round trip. Is a 10-day earnings drift in a large-cap chip stock big enough to clear that, or should we make fewer, larger trades?
